I will keep this year simple and practical. I am in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I will follow the pattern I trust most: winter wheat first, then summer maize on the same land. That fits my weather, my water situation, and the kind of work I know how to manage. I do not want to scatter my land across too many crops, because that makes field work, fertilizer, irrigation, and pest control harder to handle. Wheat gives me a steady grain crop through spring and early summer, and maize follows well after wheat harvest and makes full use of the rainy season. I will use improved or hybrid seed because I want stable yield and better resistance. I will fertilize enough to support yield but not push too hard, because fertilizer costs money and too much nitrogen can cause lodging and waste. I will use rotary tillage because it is fast, familiar, and suits my usual field preparation. I will irrigate wheat more than maize, because wheat here depends more on timely watering, while summer maize can use more rainfall. I will spray only as needed but I still plan for basic weed, disease, and insect control so I do not lose yield.
